title: D3 v2: Planner as a function — the daemon invokes a fresh headless Planner only at decision points, only when no Planner session is attached (spec round 2 after T-0182; supersedes T-0122)
spec:
Why: the interactive Planner spent about 11.2M tokens on 2026-09-18 and session 2 repeated the pattern; most of it was re-sending a large context on wait notifications. Round 2 folds in spec review T-0182: handover.py now exists on goal/T-0109 (D0 rebase); the daemon must never launch a decision Planner while an interactive Planner session is attached; no repo-generic root parameter; account and budget checked before launch; the launch step shared with goals.start.

goals.py (additive refactor): extract the launch step of start() into `launch_planner(repo_path, prompt, account_id, max_budget_usd, log_path, extra_env=None) -> dict` (trust_workspace, env incl. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN / ORCH_ROOT / filtered target secrets via the existing _filter_target_secrets + resolve_secrets, argv with --model models.planner, --output-format json, --max-budget-usd, --mcp-config .mcp.planner.json, --strict-mcp-config, --append-system-prompt <planner.md>, --dangerously-skip-permissions, Popen start_new_session, stdout+stderr to log_path); start() calls it; behaviour and tests unchanged (tests/test_goals.py stays green, one new test that start() goes through launch_planner).

orchestrator/planner_runs.py (works on ROOT only; bus.py binds one STATE per process): decision_points() scans the bus for goals (parentless triage tasks not done) and yields (goal_id, kind, payload_key) for: "scouts_done" when the goal has scout children, all are done or failed, no execute child exists yet and no run of this kind is recorded for the goal; "held" for each execute child with status held and no run recorded for (goal, task, hold_reason); "closable" when every execute child is merged, no queued or running children remain, and no run of kind closable exists. run(goal_id, kind, payload_key): (a) ATTACHED-SESSION GUARD: skip with reason "planner session attached" when the daemon runs inside an MCP server of an interactive session (mcp.py's autostart sets env ORCH_DAEMON_HOST=mcp before start_background; a standalone `orchestrator daemon` leaves it unset) or when .orchestrator/planner_session.json exists with a live pid (the resume/orchestrate skills may write it later; treat a stale pid as absent); also skip when goals.status() shows a running Planner for ROOT via identity(); (b) ACCOUNT GUARD: acct = Pool().pick("planner"); None → skip with reason "no account with headroom" (respects cooldowns, daily budget and the planner reserve); (c) handover.write(f"decision {kind}"); (d) prompt from .orchestrator/prompts/planner-decision.md ({{kind}}, {{goal_id}}, {{payload}}: "Read .orchestrator/plan.md and the bus. Decision: <kind> for <goal_id>. Do only what this decision needs, write plan.md, and finish."); (e) goals.launch_planner(ROOT, prompt, acct.id, limits.max_budget_usd.get("planner_decision", 3), runs/planner-decision-<goal_id>-<kind>.log); (f) record {goal_id, kind, payload_key, pid, started_at, account, log, skipped_reason?} in .orchestrator/runs/planner_runs.json under bus.locked(); skips are recorded too (so a skipped decision is retried next tick only when the skip reason was a guard, never when it already launched).
daemon.tick(): after the stages, when pool.cfg.get("planner", {}).get("autonomous", False) is true, iterate decision_points() and run at most one launch per tick, wrapped like the stages. pool.toml: `[planner] autonomous = false` with a comment (default off: the interactive Planner owns decisions; turn on only in the executor container) and `planner_decision = 3.0` in limits.max_budget_usd. mcp.py: set os.environ["ORCH_DAEMON_HOST"] = "mcp" before daemon.start_background (one line). README.md: a paragraph "Autonomous decisions" under Pipeline.
Tests tests/test_planner_runs.py (harness): decision_points_scouts_done_held_closable (three fixtures), run_skips_when_session_attached (env ORCH_DAEMON_HOST=mcp → no Popen, skip recorded), run_skips_without_account_headroom (pick patched to None), run_launches_once_per_decision (launch_planner patched; second tick no relaunch), tick_launches_nothing_when_autonomous_false (default cfg), plus tests/test_goals.py: start_uses_launch_planner. No new dependency; commit on the task branch when green. Finish with: summary, files changed, failures-only test output.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_runs.py has the five named tests and tests/test_goals.py the launch_planner test; all green; existing goals and daemon tests untouched and green
With [planner] autonomous = false (committed default) tick() launches nothing; with it true and ORCH_DAEMON_HOST=mcp nothing launches either (skip recorded)
planner_runs.json records one entry per (goal, kind, payload_key); a second tick does not relaunch a launched decision; guard skips are retried
goals.start behaviour unchanged and routed through launch_planner (secrets filter preserved); mcp.py sets ORCH_DAEMON_HOST=mcp before autostart
uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests green; no new dependency; only the eight scoped files change; committed on the task branch

constraints.scope_note: nine files by Planner decision: the shared launch helper lives in goals.py and the session flag in mcp.py

result.summary: superseded by D3 v3 (next id after T-0188): spec review T-0188 requested changes (held dedup key reused across fix rounds so later holds are never retried; no reconciliation of a dead decision Planner; the goals.status() guard clause never applies to ROOT; planner_session.json guard untested; payload_key undefined for scouts_done/closable). Recreated.

spec_review_risks.issue: The 'held' dedup key is (goal, task, hold_reason), but hold_reason strings are static and reused across independent rounds (daemon.py:275 'spec_review request_changes', daemon.py:331 'worktree missing', daemon.py:336 'gate_red'). Once a decision run is recorded for that tuple, a genuinely new hold on the same task with the same reason in a later fix round is silently skipped forever — exactly the multi-round scenario CLAUDE.md's escalation policy ('Executor fails 3 rounds on one criterion') exists to catch, except autonomous mode stops trying after round 1.

No reconciliation exists for a decision-Planner process that dies before finishing. goals.py already solves this exact class of problem for regular goal launches via identity()/_reconcile() (dead pid -> status exited). Here, once run() records an entry with no skipped_reason, decision_points() treats it as permanently done regardless of whether the launched Planner actually completed — a crashed/killed decision Planner leaves that (goal, kind, payload_key) stuck with no retry path.

The attached-session guard's second clause ('goals.status() shows a running Planner for ROOT via identity()') checks a mechanism that likely never applies to ROOT: goals.start()/status() track headless Planner sessions launched against target repos via serve.py/cli.py, while the actual interactive session on ROOT is launched out-of-band via the `f orch` shell function (README.md:28), which never calls goals.start() against ROOT. This clause probably always finds no record, giving false assurance that two independent guards exist when only the ORCH_DAEMON_HOST check is live.

The five named tests cover only the ORCH_DAEMON_HOST=mcp half of the attached-session guard (run_skips_when_session_attached). No named test exercises the .orchestrator/planner_session.json live-pid branch, so half of a safety-critical guard (the one meant to prevent a second Planner racing an attached interactive one) ships unverified by the stated acceptance criteria.

payload_key is only unambiguous for 'held' (task_id + hold_reason). For 'scouts_done' and 'closable' the spec doesn't say what payload_key should be, leaving the dedup key's shape to implementer judgment and risking an inconsistent convention between kinds.
